data.title: bn-1kw: Adopt an Apollo-derived 64-color console palette
data.description: For bn-1kw: replaced the 16-color runtime with a reproducible Apollo-derived 64-color palette; widened draw/display/transparency/web/agent surfaces; introduced explicit fillp secondary colors; migrated sprite and screen text alphabets; recolored and browser-validated Lantern Leap. risk:high — failure-mode checklist required. Please answer: 1) What failure modes exist? 2) What edge cases need validation? 3) How can we roll back if this breaks? 4) What monitoring/alerts should we add? 5) What input validation is needed?

data.body: LOW (defense-in-depth): this PALETTE index (and lines 441 and 1532) dropped the previous `& 15` guard, so it now reads PALETTE[usize::from(v)] unmasked. It is safe today because every sprite byte reaches these paths through parse_color_char / sprite poke, which bound values to 0..=63, and PALETTE now has 64 entries. But the inline guarantee is gone: any future sprite-byte source that skips that validation (a raw/binary sprite load, or an unvalidated saved-state restore) would turn an out-of-range byte into a panic here instead of a harmless wrong color. console-core's own remap()/encode_png still mask with COLOR_MASK — masking these three sites the same way keeps the render infallible and self-enforcing.

INFO (failure-mode 1/5 — What could fail in production?): This is a 16->64 index-width migration touching every color path. Highest-risk failure classes: (a) an OOB index/panic if any color-index array access was missed — verified NONE remain in console-core: all draw_pal/display_pal/palt/remap/cls sites mask with COLOR_MASK, and the u16->u64 palt widening correctly covers transparency bits for indices 16..63. (b) A stale/mismatched web engine: template.html now sizes pal/lut from con_color_count(), but an OLD cached engine.js/wasm lacking the con_color_count export leaves COLOR_COUNT undefined -> NaN sizing -> blank/garbled canvas. (c) Old 16-color carts still parse fine (0-f are the first 16 alphabet chars), so no data loss. Framebuffer stays byte-safe: masked to 0..=63 on every write and again in encode_png and the JS shell.

INFO (failure-mode 2/5 — How would we detect it quickly?): Native/agent OOB would surface immediately as a Rust panic in logs/CI (seconds). The web smoke (web/smoke.cjs) now asserts con_color_count()===64, palette length COLOR_COUNT*3, and that every stepped framebuffer index is < COLOR_COUNT (this line) — run it in CI against a freshly built engine.js to catch a stale-ABI mismatch before ship. Gap: there is no runtime signal for the browser shell in the field, so a stale cached engine would render wrong for end users with nothing server-side to alert on. Recommend a one-time console assert in template.html when con_color_count is missing or !=64, plus content-hashed engine asset filenames so browsers cannot pin an old wasm.

INFO (failure-mode 3/5 — What is the fastest safe rollback?): Pure code/data change, no schema or persisted-state migration, so rollback = revert this commit and rebuild (native + web/build-engine.sh). Estimate minutes. Caveat: any cart re-authored to use colors 16..63 (e.g. the recolored Lantern Leap) renders those indices masked back into 0..15 under the reverted engine — visually wrong but NOT a crash and NOT data loss, since the cart text is unchanged. No user data is persisted in a 64-color-dependent format, so there is nothing to unwind. The browser rollback only actually takes effect quickly if the engine asset is cache-busted (see failure-mode 2) — otherwise clients keep the new wasm from cache.

INFO (failure-mode 4/5 — What dependency could invalidate this plan?): (a) The web shell<->engine ABI: the new con_color_count export must be present in the deployed wasm; a partial deploy (new HTML + old wasm, or the reverse) breaks rendering — keep template.html and engine.js/wasm versioned and deployed together. (b) COLOR_MASK = COLOR_COUNT - 1 (defined here, and identically in Rust) is a bitmask that is ONLY correct because 64 is a power of two; if COLOR_COUNT ever becomes non-power-of-two, every '& COLOR_MASK' silently mis-maps instead of clamping. Worth a compile-time/startup assert that COLOR_COUNT is a power of two. (c) tools/apollo64.mjs is the source of truth for the baked PALETTE constant; it runs on Node with no inputs and only console.log output (no file writes, no shell exec — no injection surface), but the emitted table and the hand-copied Rust constant can drift. A CI check that regenerates and diffs would keep them in sync.

INFO (failure-mode 5/5 — What assumption is least certain?): The weakest link is the invariant 'every sprite/framebuffer byte is already in 0..=63.' console-core enforces it by masking on every write and the cart parser enforces it via parse_color_char, but sprite/view.rs now indexes PALETTE[usize::from(v)] WITHOUT an inline mask (see the LOW note on lines 405/441/1532), so it trusts that invariant rather than enforcing it locally. Correct today; it is the assumption most likely to break silently if a future non-text sprite-load or saved-state restore path is added, at which point a bad byte becomes a panic in the agent renderer instead of a masked wrong color. Masking those three sites with '& COLOR_MASK' would make the assumption self-enforcing and eliminate the only place an out-of-range byte can crash.

data.reason: Security review complete. No memory-safety or injection vulnerabilities: every color-index access in console-core masks with COLOR_MASK, the palt bitmask was correctly widened u16->u64 for indices 16..63, the framebuffer is byte-bounded on write and again at scanout (encode_png + JS shell), and apollo64.mjs is a build-time tool with no inputs/file-writes/shell-exec. One LOW defense-in-depth note (unmasked PALETTE indexing in sprite/view.rs relies on the parse invariant) and the required risk:high failure-mode checklist are attached as non-blocking comments.

data.body: Fixed in f638cc3: all three sprite-renderer PALETTE reads now mask with COLOR_MASK before indexing; focused clippy and sprite-view tests pass.

Addressed the mask assumption in f638cc3 with a compile-time COLOR_COUNT.is_power_of_two() assertion. The packed HTML embeds the matching engine and shell together; web smoke verifies con_color_count()==64.
Fixed in f638cc3: the renderer invariant is now self-enforcing at every PALETTE read. Also added a compile-time assertion that COLOR_COUNT is a power of two.
